implementation_notes: kotlin.sequences.generateSequence(seed, nextFunction) is the standard-library unfold: the next-function returns the following state or null to stop, and the result is a lazily evaluated Sequence that is walked on demand by for, take or first. The sequence { } builder with yield/yieldAll covers what the next-function shape cannot express - a step that emits several layers, or generation driven by a loop with side conditions - and generateSequence with only a next-function adapts an external source into a Sequence. Neither is memoised, so every traversal recomputes the unfold.
pitfalls: A Sequence is cold and unmemoised: iterating it twice runs the step function twice (and repeats its side effects), unlike a List.
A null seed is treated as an empty sequence, so a legitimately null first element is silently dropped.
A step function that never returns null generates forever; there is no fuel or cycle detection, so bounding is the caller's job.
